steps: Shape your dominant hand into an open hand with the thumb extended outward.
Touch your thumb firmly against the side of your forehead near the temple.
Sweep your hand straight down until the thumb lands flat on your chest.
Keep your palm angled toward your opposite side while the hand travels downward.
Hold a neutral, matter-of-fact expression, since the sign needs no special facial grammar.
tip: Lifeprint glosses this one sign as MAN, BOY, GUY, DUDE and FELLOW — context picks the English word.

steps: Shape both hands into loose open-F handshapes, each thumb tip resting against its index fingertip.
Hold your hands apart in the signing space in front of your chest.
Bring both hands toward each other and hook the fingers together into interlocking F shapes.
Angle your palms toward each other so the hooked fingers cross like two chain links.
End with a brief firm hold, adding a small nod when used as a statement.
tip: The same sign also covers JOIN, OF, MEMBER and OWN — let the sentence decide which English word fits.

steps: Hold both hands in slightly curved B handshapes, thumbs resting alongside the palms.
Start low in front of your torso with the fingertips of both hands nearly touching at the center.
Sweep both hands upward and outward in matching arcs to outline the basket's widening sides.
Keep your palms facing inward toward each other through the whole tracing motion.
Finish with your hands apart at roughly shoulder width, glancing at the shape you outlined.
tip: Scale the sign to the basket — a tall laundry hamper gets the same motion drawn taller and narrower.

steps: Form your dominant hand into an index-finger handshape with the other fingers folded down.
Hold your non-dominant hand out in front of you, flat and palm up, as a base.
Slide your dominant index finger forward across the base palm from wrist toward fingertips.
Without pausing, repeat the same forward slide across the palm a second time.
Keep the dominant palm facing down during both passes and a neutral expression.
tip: Repeating the sign turns WEEK into WEEKLY — ASL marks 'every' by doubling time signs.

steps: Hold both hands flat with the fingers together and palms facing each other.
Raise both hands to the sides of your head near your ears, like blinders on a horse.
Push both hands a short distance forward and away from your head.
Keep your palms facing inward toward each other through the whole forward push.
Direct a steady gaze toward the person you are addressing to reinforce the meaning.
tip: Reverse the direction — pull toward your own face — when you are calling for someone to pay attention to you.

steps: Raise both hands with the index fingers extended and the other fingers folded into fists.
Start at the top-left corner of the shape in the signing space before your chest.
Trace the outline of a square: right, then down, then left, then back up.
Keep your fingertips pointing forward and your palms angled slightly toward each other.
Use a confident neutral expression, mouthing the word lightly only if it helps clarity.
tip: The same sign also means BOARD and BILLBOARD — the sentence tells listeners which one you mean.
